newsitem.title: USA: NASA resets U.S. shuttle landing for Friday.
newsitem.headline: NASA resets U.S. shuttle landing for Friday.

text.p: NASA's mission control called off Thursday's planned Florida homecoming of the space shuttle Columbia and rescheduled the landing for Friday.
Cloudy skies at the shuttle's home base in Florida forced the U.S. space agency to wave off Columbia on two landing opportunities.
"We are going to call it a day ... for trying to get home and we are going to plan for tomorrow," mission control's Curt Brown told the astronauts.
The shuttle's touchdown was rescheduled for 8:01 a.m. EST (1301 GMT) on Friday at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre. There were also opportunities to land in California if necessary.

The weather was expected to improve on Friday, contrary to an earlier forecast which had caused the National Aeronautics and Space Administration to order the shuttle home one day earlier than planned.
The delay will make Columbia's mission the second longest shuttle flight ever.
